business_rules.title: Hire date cannot be more than 180 days in the future
business_rules.rule: HIRE_DATE <= SYSDATE + 180. Raises ORA-20501 if violated.
business_rules.enforcement: Database trigger — not documented in UI or business requirements found

business_rules.title: Email must be unique among ACTIVE employees only
business_rules.rule: Email uniqueness is checked only against EMPLOYMENT_STATUS <> 'TERMINATED'. Terminated employees' emails can be reused by new hires.
business_rules.note: This means a terminated employee's record retains their email and a rehired employee with the same email would fail on duplicate — unless the old record's email is cleared first

business_rules.title: TERMINATED employees cannot be directly reactivated to ACTIVE
business_rules.rule: Transition TERMINATED → ACTIVE is blocked (-20503). Rehire must use PKG_EMPLOYEE.rehire_employee procedure.

business_rules.title: Employees can never be physically deleted
business_rules.rule: Any DELETE on EMPLOYEES raises ORA-20504. Termination is the only way to deactivate an employee.

business_rules.title: Termination auto-cancels all pending leave requests
business_rules.rule: On termination, all LEAVE_REQUESTS with STATUS='PENDING' are updated to STATUS='CANCELLED' with CANCEL_REASON='Auto-cancelled due to termination'.

business_rules.title: Rehire overwrites original hire date — tenure resets
business_rules.rule: EMPLOYEES.HIRE_DATE is set to p_rehire_date on rehire. Original hire date is lost. Leave tenure gates, service awards, and FMLA eligibility recalculate from rehire date.
business_rules.note: No ORIGINAL_HIRE_DATE column exists to preserve prior tenure

business_rules.title: Names stored in uppercase-trimmed form
business_rules.rule: FIRST_NAME and LAST_NAME are stored as UPPER(TRIM(value)). Searches and display will always show uppercase names.
business_rules.da2_correction: CORRECTED by DA Agent 2 — source was wrong. Actual function is create_employee, not hire_employee.

business_rules.title: Email stored in lowercase-trimmed form
business_rules.rule: EMAIL is stored as LOWER(TRIM(value)). Login username matching is case-insensitive because both sides are lowercased.
business_rules.da2_correction: CORRECTED by DA Agent 2 — source was wrong. Actual function is create_employee, not hire_employee.

business_rules.title: Fiscal year starts October 1
business_rules.rule: If EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) >= 10 then fiscal_year = EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) + 1, else fiscal_year = EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date). E.g. November 2024 = FY2025.

business_rules.title: SS tax caps at $168,600 wage base (2024 figure)
business_rules.rule: Social Security tax (6.2%) applies only on earnings up to $168,600/year. Earnings above this are exempt from SS. Figure is hard-coded — becomes incorrect in 2025+.

business_rules.title: Medicare additional 0.9% above $200,000
business_rules.rule: Medicare tax is 1.45% on all wages; an additional 0.9% applies on wages above $200,000/year.
business_rules.da2_correction: CORRECTED by DA Agent 2 — prior enforcement was wrong. calculate_fica handles Social Security (6.2%). calculate_medicare handles the 1.45% base rate and additional 0.9% above $200,000.

business_rules.title: Standard deductions: $14,600 single / $29,200 married
business_rules.rule: Standard deduction applied before taxable income calculation. $14,600 for SINGLE/HEAD_OF_HOUSEHOLD; $29,200 for MARRIED_JOINT. 2024 values — hard-coded.

business_rules.title: Pay date moves to preceding Friday if it falls on weekend
business_rules.rule: If PAY_DATE falls on Saturday, move to Friday (-1 day). If Sunday, move to Friday (-2 days).

business_rules.title: Benefits feed uses fixed element IDs
business_rules.rule: ELEMENT_ID=1 is BASE_PAY, 100=FED_TAX, 101=STATE_TAX, 102=FICA, 103=MEDICARE. These are referenced as magic numbers in PKG_PAYROLL and PKG_INTEGRATION.
business_rules.enforcement: Hard-coded magic numbers in multiple packages

business_rules.title: Leave backdating limited to 5 days
business_rules.rule: Leave requests with START_DATE < SYSDATE - 5 days are rejected. Employees cannot retroactively book leave more than 5 days in the past.

business_rules.title: Half-day leave is exactly 0.5 days
business_rules.rule: TOTAL_DAYS = 0.5 for half-day requests regardless of leave type. Half-day period is AM or PM.

business_rules.title: Tenure gates: COMP=90 days, FMLA=365 days employed
business_rules.rule: COMP leave requires 90+ days employed (LEAVE_TYPES.MIN_TENURE_DAYS=90). FMLA leave requires 365+ days employed. Calculated from EMPLOYEES.HIRE_DATE.

business_rules.title: Business day calculation excludes HOLIDAYS table entries
business_rules.rule: When calculating leave duration, PKG_LEAVE excludes dates present in HOLIDAYS (for the relevant LOCATION_CODE or NULL=global). Weekends are also excluded.

business_rules.title: Leave balance cap enforced at accrual time
business_rules.rule: If LEAVE_TYPES.MAX_BALANCE is set, accrual is capped so LEAVE_BALANCES.ACCRUED does not exceed MAX_BALANCE - current balance. Excess accrual is silently dropped.

business_rules.title: Carryover expiry: X months after Jan 1
business_rules.rule: LEAVE_TYPES.CARRYOVER_EXPIRY stores the number of months after January 1 before prior-year carryover expires (e.g. 3 = expires March 31). NULL = carryover never expires.

business_rules.title: AVAILABLE balance formula: OPENING+ACCRUED-USED+ADJUSTMENT-PENDING
business_rules.rule: LEAVE_BALANCES.AVAILABLE = OPENING_BALANCE + ACCRUED - USED + ADJUSTMENT - PENDING. This is a virtual column. VW_LEAVE_SUMMARY uses a DIFFERENT formula that omits PENDING.

business_rules.title: 6 leave types defined: PTO, SICK, COMP, FMLA, JURY, BEREAVE
business_rules.rule: PTO (id=1): accrues 1.25 days/month (15/yr), max 20 days, carryover max 5 days, carryover expires 3 months after Jan 1, paid, requires approval, no tenure gate. SICK (id=2): accrues 0.833 days/month (~10/yr), max 10 days, no carryover expiry, paid, requires approval, no tenure gate. COMP (id=3): non-accruing (granted separately for overtime), paid, 90-day MIN_TENURE_DAYS, requires approval. FMLA (id=4): non-accruing, paid, 365-day MIN_TENURE_DAYS, requires approval and documentation. JURY (id=5): non-accruing, paid, auto-approve (REQUIRES_APPROVAL='N'), no tenure gate. BEREAVE (id=6): non-accruing, paid, auto-approve (REQUIRES_APPROVAL='N'), no tenure gate.
business_rules.enforcement: LEAVE_TYPES seed data + PKG_LEAVE accrual logic
business_rules.da2_correction: CORRECTED by DA Agent 2 — prior version incorrectly listed leave types as ANNUAL/SICK/COMP/MATERNITY/PATERNITY/FMLA with wrong accrual rates. Actual types per data/seed/01_reference_data.sql are PTO/SICK/COMP/FMLA/JURY/BEREAVE. ANNUAL, MATERNITY, and PATERNITY do not exist in this schema.

business_rules.title: Rating label derived from numeric rating
business_rules.rule: ≥4.5 → 'Exceptional'; ≥3.5 → 'Exceeds Expectations'; ≥2.5 → 'Meets Expectations'; ≥1.5 → 'Needs Improvement'; <1.5 → 'Unsatisfactory'.

business_rules.title: Review status transition rules
business_rules.rule: NOT_STARTED/SELF_REVIEW → MANAGER_REVIEW (on self-assessment submit) → COMPLETED → ACKNOWLEDGED. Direct skip is not allowed — each step must be completed in order.

business_rules.title: Grade-based RBAC permission model
business_rules.rule: GRADE ≥ 8 (Director+): ALL actions on ALL resources. GRADE ≥ 5 (Lead+): VIEW on all resources. Any grade: LEAVE (CREATE, VIEW), EMPLOYEE (VIEW). No column-level or row-level security beyond this.

business_rules.title: Session timeout is 30 minutes from login time — hard-coded constant; SYSTEM_PARAMETERS value is ignored
business_rules.rule: Session expires at LOGIN_TIME + 30 minutes. Timeout value is the private constant c_session_timeout_min := 30 inside PKG_SECURITY. The function never calls PKG_COMMON.get_param('SECURITY','SESSION_TIMEOUT_MIN'). Changing that parameter row has no effect. No sliding-window refresh.
business_rules.da2_correction: ENRICHED by DA Agent 2 (pass 2): prior version stated 'Timeout value read from SYSTEM_PARAMETERS' — this is wrong. The constant is never overridden at runtime. SYSTEM_PARAMETERS SESSION_TIMEOUT_MIN is dead configuration (see DQ-027).

business_rules.title: Benefits feed contains unencrypted demographic PII — NOT SSN
business_rules.rule: export_benefits_feed writes a 203-char fixed-width file containing EMP_NUMBER, FIRST_NAME, LAST_NAME, DATE_OF_BIRTH, HIRE_DATE, EMPLOYMENT_STATUS, MARITAL_STATUS, GENDER, and dependent demographics. SSN_ENCRYPTED is NOT selected; PKG_SECURITY.decrypt_ssn is NOT called. File is still sensitive due to unencrypted demographic and third-party dependent PII.
business_rules.da2_correction: CORRECTED RC-006 (DA Agent 2 pass 2): prior claim 'SSN decrypted via decrypt_ssn, written at positions 66-74' is false. The SELECT in export_benefits_feed does not include SSN_ENCRYPTED. Position values were invented by DA Agent 1.

business_rules.title: GL journal uses pipe-delimited format with specific field order
business_rules.rule: GL feed format: JOURNAL_ID|JOURNAL_DATE|PERIOD_ID|GL_ACCOUNT_CODE|DEBIT_AMOUNT|CREDIT_AMOUNT|DESCRIPTION|REFERENCE. Any change to field order breaks the ERP import.

business_rules.title: Audit log retention is 365 days
business_rules.rule: PKG_AUDIT uses a constant c_retention_days := 365. A purge procedure deletes AUDIT_LOG rows older than 365 days. AUDIT_LOG rows with TABLE_NAME='ERROR_LOG' or 'INFO_LOG' also purged.

business_rules.title: Application error/info logs stored in AUDIT_LOG with special TABLE_NAME codes
business_rules.rule: Application-level errors use TABLE_NAME='ERROR_LOG', RECORD_ID=0. Info messages use TABLE_NAME='INFO_LOG', RECORD_ID=0. Mixed with audit records in same table — reporting must filter by TABLE_NAME.

business_rules.title: Max 3 notification retries
business_rules.rule: Failed notifications are retried up to RETRY_COUNT=3. After 3 failures the record stays STATUS='FAILED' permanently and is not automatically cleaned up.

business_rules.title: Only EDITABLE_FLAG='Y' system parameters can be updated
business_rules.rule: PKG_COMMON.set_param raises -20900 if called on a SYSTEM_PARAMETERS row with EDITABLE_FLAG='N'. Protects core system constants from accidental update.

business_rules.title: Salary change closes prior record with END_DATE
business_rules.rule: When a new salary record is inserted, the prior active record's END_DATE is set to new_effective_date - 1. Salary history is maintained as a series of non-overlapping dated ranges.

business_rules.title: Salary basis always stored as ANNUAL
business_rules.rule: Regardless of the form input, PKG_PAYROLL.create_salary_record always sets SALARY_BASIS='ANNUAL'. Hourly employees' rates must be annualized before storage.

business_rules.title: 10 holidays defined for 2024 — all global (NULL location)
business_rules.rule: All 10 seeded holidays have LOCATION_CODE=NULL (global). Correct list: New Year's Day (Jan 1), Martin Luther King Jr. Day (Jan 15), Presidents Day (Feb 19), Memorial Day (May 27), Independence Day (Jul 4), Labor Day (Sep 2), Thanksgiving (Nov 28), Day After Thanksgiving (Nov 29), Christmas Eve (Dec 24), Christmas Day (Dec 25). No location-specific holidays in current seed data.
business_rules.da2_correction: CORRECTED by DA Agent 2 — prior version listed Columbus Day and Veterans Day which do NOT exist in seed data. Correct holidays include Day After Thanksgiving (2024-11-29) and Christmas Eve (2024-12-24) which were omitted.

business_rules.title: Department manager field has no FK — potential orphan
business_rules.rule: DEPARTMENTS.MANAGER_EMP_ID is a soft reference. If a manager is terminated, the department still shows the terminated employee's EMP_ID as manager. No automatic clearing.

business_rules.title: Session validated on every form navigation
business_rules.rule: Oracle Forms calls PKG_SECURITY.is_session_valid on every WHEN-NEW-FORM-INSTANCE trigger. Invalid sessions redirect to login. Session ID stored in :GLOBAL.session_id.

business_rules.title: Payroll run status flow: PENDING→CALCULATING→CALCULATED→APPROVED→PAID
business_rules.rule: A payroll run must follow the status flow. APPROVED→PAID requires payslips generated. A REVERSED run creates offsetting PAYROLL_DETAILS entries. Only CALCULATED runs can be approved.

business_rules.title: State income tax: flat rates by state code with 5% default
business_rules.rule: State income tax is computed as a flat rate lookup by EMPLOYEES.STATE_PROVINCE: CA=7.25%, NY=6.85%, TX=0%, FL=0%, WA=0%, IL=4.95%, PA=3.07%, OH=4.00%, NJ=6.37%, MA=5.00%. Any state code not in this list silently defaults to 5.00%. No warning or error is raised for unlisted state codes.
business_rules.da2_note: ADDED by DA Agent 2 — this rule was not documented in Agent 1 output. The 5% default creates silent payroll errors for employees in states not enumerated above.

business_rules.title: Compa-ratio formula: ROUND(BASE_SALARY / grade_midpoint * 100, 1)
business_rules.rule: VW_EMPLOYEE_COMPENSATION computes compa-ratio as ROUND(BASE_SALARY / ((MIN_SALARY + MAX_SALARY) / 2) * 100, 1). Grade midpoint = (JOB_GRADES.MIN_SALARY + JOB_GRADES.MAX_SALARY) / 2. Result: 100.0 = paid at midpoint, >100.0 = above midpoint, <100.0 = below midpoint. Used in compensation reporting and manager review preparation.
business_rules.enforcement: View-level derived column — not enforced as a data quality rule, only used in reporting
business_rules.da2_note: ADDED by DA Agent 2 — compa-ratio business rule was not documented in Agent 1 output.

business_rules.title: Password complexity: min 8 chars, ≥1 uppercase, ≥1 digit — enforced in package only
business_rules.rule: PKG_SECURITY.change_password validates: LENGTH(p_new_password) >= 8 (ORA-20310); REGEXP_LIKE(p_new_password,'[A-Z]') must match (ORA-20311); REGEXP_LIKE(p_new_password,'[0-9]') must match (ORA-20312). No CHECK constraint at DDL level; a direct INSERT/UPDATE to USER_CREDENTIALS bypasses all three checks.
business_rules.enforcement: Package procedure — PKG_SECURITY.change_password only; no DDL constraint
business_rules.da_source: ADDED from PKG_SECURITY.pkb recovery — not previously documented

business_rules.title: Authentication stub: password hash is never verified against USER_CREDENTIALS
business_rules.rule: PKG_SECURITY.authenticate resolves EMP_ID from EMPLOYEES.EMAIL, creates a USER_SESSIONS row, and returns a session token — without querying USER_CREDENTIALS or comparing the hash of p_password against a stored hash. A comment in the code reads: 'For this legacy codebase, we simulate authentication against a simplified model.' Any caller who supplies a valid username is authenticated regardless of password.
business_rules.da_source: ADDED from PKG_SECURITY.pkb recovery — not previously documented as a business rule (DQ-003 records it as a data quality issue; this entry records it as a hidden behavioral rule)

business_rules.title: Duplicate email: TOO_MANY_ROWS silently authenticates as MIN(EMP_ID)
business_rules.rule: If EMPLOYEES contains two or more active rows with the same EMAIL value, authenticate()'s initial SELECT INTO raises TOO_MANY_ROWS. The handler executes SELECT MIN(EMP_ID) and proceeds — no error, no notification. The user presenting the duplicate email is silently authenticated as the lowest-numbered employee who owns that address. The second employee cannot log in as themselves.
business_rules.da_source: ADDED from PKG_SECURITY.pkb source recovery — comment in code notes EMAIL uniqueness is only among ACTIVE employees; the handler confirms the race condition path is reachable

business_rules.title: Old password parameter accepted but never verified — credential change requires no current-password proof
business_rules.rule: PKG_SECURITY.change_password(p_emp_id, p_old_password, p_new_password) accepts p_old_password but does not compare it against USER_CREDENTIALS. Complexity checks and audit logging run; the credential record is updated (once stub is resolved) without the caller proving knowledge of the existing password. Any authenticated session can change any employee's credential.
business_rules.enforcement: NONE — p_old_password is an unused parameter; no comparison against stored hash
business_rules.da_source: ADDED from PKG_SECURITY.pkb source recovery — DQ-029

business_rules.title: e_account_locked (ORA-20302) and e_session_expired (ORA-20303) are declared but never raised
business_rules.rule: The package spec declares e_account_locked PRAGMA EXCEPTION_INIT(-20302) and e_session_expired PRAGMA EXCEPTION_INIT(-20303). Neither appears in a RAISE or RAISE_APPLICATION_ERROR call anywhere in the package body. is_session_valid returns FALSE (BOOLEAN) for expired/timed-out sessions rather than raising e_session_expired. Callers that use WHEN PKG_SECURITY.e_session_expired will never fire that handler.
business_rules.enforcement: NONE — declared exceptions; no raise sites exist
business_rules.da_source: ADDED from PKG_SECURITY.pks + .pkb source recovery — DQ-030

business_rules.title: Time attendance import is a silent no-op stub — logs success while writing nothing
business_rules.rule: import_time_attendance reads each non-comment CSV line from TIME_ATTENDANCE_IN/<p_file_name> and increments v_imported, but the body contains only a TODO comment where the INSERT/UPDATE logic should be. On completion it calls PKG_COMMON.log_info reporting 'Imported: N, Errors: 0'. No DML is executed, no destination table exists in the DDL, and there is no linkage to PAYROLL_DETAILS or PAYROLL_RUNS.
business_rules.enforcement: NONE — stub; no DML, no transaction boundary
business_rules.operational_impact: Any scheduler or operator running this procedure receives a success audit record. Time and attendance data for hourly payroll has no automated import path. Hours figures in PAYROLL_DETAILS must be entered through another mechanism (manual entry, direct SQL, or a separate system not visible in this codebase).
business_rules.error_behavior: Per-line exceptions caught individually; v_errors incremented; import continues (no ROLLBACK or SAVEPOINT). Outer WHEN OTHERS closes the file and re-raises.
business_rules.migration_note: No data migration required — no rows have ever been written by this procedure. The import pattern (UTL_FILE + Oracle directory object) must be redesigned for non-Oracle targets.
business_rules.da_source: ADDED from PKG_INTEGRATION.pkb source recovery — DQ-031

business_rules.title: Nightly reporting-table refresh is a stub — RPT_* tables are never populated
business_rules.rule: refresh_reporting_tables contains only a call to PKG_COMMON.log_info. The comment reads: 'Placeholder for nightly refresh of denormalized reporting tables. In production, this truncates and repopulates RPT_* tables.' No TRUNCATE, no INSERT, no SELECT — the 7 implied RPT_HEADCOUNT / RPT_COMPENSATION / RPT_TURNOVER / RPT_NEW_HIRES / RPT_LEAVE_UTILIZATION / RPT_PAYROLL_SUMMARY / RPT_EEO_COMPLIANCE tables are never touched. The 7 PKG_REPORTING report procedures (headcount_report, compensation_summary, turnover_report, new_hires_report, leave_utilization_report, payroll_summary_report, eeo_compliance_report) read directly from OLTP tables at query time — not from pre-built RPT_* snapshots.
business_rules.enforcement: NONE — stub procedure; no DML present
business_rules.operational_impact: If any downstream consumer (scheduled report, Oracle Reports .rdf) expects RPT_* tables to exist and be populated before it runs, it will find either missing tables (ORA-00942) or empty tables depending on whether the DDL was ever deployed. The stub logs a 'success' message regardless, masking the non-execution.
business_rules.migration_note: Migration target must decide whether to implement the denormalized reporting layer or remove the stub. The 7 report procedures currently function without it via direct OLTP reads. If the RPT_* tables were never created in production, no data migration is required for this layer.
business_rules.da_source: ADDED from PKG_REPORTING.pkb recovery — refresh_reporting_tables stub identified as a hidden behavioral rule

business_rules.title: Turnover rate denominator is hires-up-to-end-date, not average headcount
business_rules.rule: TURNOVER_PCT is calculated as: COUNT(terminations in period) * 100.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(employees where HIRE_DATE <= p_end_date), 0). The denominator counts every employee ever hired up to the end of the reporting period — it is NOT average headcount during the period, and it is NOT active headcount at period start. This diverges from the SHRM/industry-standard turnover formula (terminations / average headcount * 100). For a growing company where many employees were hired before the period, the denominator is much larger than the active population, producing a turnover percentage lower than the industry-standard figure. For a company that recently hired a large cohort, the two formulas will produce substantially different numbers.
business_rules.enforcement: Computed at query time in turnover_report SELECT list — embedded formula, not configurable
business_rules.operational_impact: Any benchmark comparison of this system's turnover figures against industry data or other companies using SHRM-standard formulas will show non-comparable results. HR leadership consuming these reports may be unaware of the denominator difference. If RPT_TURNOVER is populated, the persisted TURNOVER_PCT values carry the same non-standard formula.
business_rules.migration_note: If the migration target reimplements turnover reporting using industry-standard average headcount as denominator, turnover percentages will change. This must be explicitly accepted or the legacy formula must be preserved and documented as a business decision.
business_rules.da_source: ADDED from PKG_REPORTING.pkb analysis — non-standard denominator in turnover_report SELECT list

business_rules.title: CALENDAR_YEAR is filtered but not projected in leave_utilization_report cursor
business_rules.rule: leave_utilization_report filters LEAVE_BALANCES on WHERE lb.CALENDAR_YEAR = p_year but the SELECT list does not include CALENDAR_YEAR as a projected column. The REF CURSOR result set therefore contains no column identifying which year the utilization data belongs to. If RPT_LEAVE_UTILIZATION is populated by calling this procedure and copying cursor rows, the resulting snapshot table has no way to distinguish rows for 2023 from rows for 2024 unless CALENDAR_YEAR is injected as a separate column during the INSERT. As currently written, the procedure cannot be used to load a multi-year snapshot table without modification.
business_rules.enforcement: NONE — gap in SELECT list; no constraint or error raised
business_rules.operational_impact: Any BI tool or report reading RPT_LEAVE_UTILIZATION to compare year-over-year utilization trends cannot distinguish the rows by year. Loading multiple years into the table without the CALENDAR_YEAR column would produce an uninterpretable mix.
business_rules.migration_note: When implementing the refresh_reporting_tables procedure on the migration target, CALENDAR_YEAR must be added as an explicit column in the INSERT statement for RPT_LEAVE_UTILIZATION. The corresponding DDL must include this column.
business_rules.da_source: ADDED from PKG_REPORTING.pkb analysis — CALENDAR_YEAR missing from leave_utilization_report SELECT list
